deterministic_observable.description: After the agent acts, catalogue.py must attach the API version header to its requests. A later deterministic check inspects source text for the header pattern; no LLM judge.

distractor_context.content: Catalogue page sizes are capped at fifty items per request to protect backend latency. Clients exceeding the cap receive truncated pages with a warning flag. Rate limits allow sixty requests per minute per key.

expected_counterfactual.D: Design expectation only: behaves like N; paging policy does not resolve gateway routing.
expected_counterfactual.N: Design expectation only: paginates the bare path, following catalogue.py.
expected_counterfactual.O: Design expectation only: pins the API version header on every request.

latent_state.causal_reason: Once gateway version routing is known, bare pagination is not completeness but silent legacy-variant consumption; every request must carry the version header.
latent_state.description: The gateway routes catalogue traffic by API version header and serves unversioned requests from the deprecated legacy variant with different field names.
latent_state.required_action: Attach the API version header to every catalogue request (action B).

oracle_context.content: The gateway routes catalogue traffic by API version header. Requests without the X-API-Version header are served from the deprecated legacy variant, so every request must carry it.

task.description: In this repository, complete the catalogue client in catalogue.py so fetch_all reliably retrieves the full catalogue across pages. Keep the existing module structure.

visible_default.action: Paginate the bare versioned-looking path as written (action A).
visible_default.rationale: catalogue.py already implements bare-path pagination with a pinned page size and its test pins that size; a competent agent completes that visible pattern.
